chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Sinan from Uthman ibn Marwan from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His saying, 'The fasting person has the choice until the sun sets,' he said, 'Indeed, that is for the obligatory fast; as for the voluntary fast, he may break his fast at any hour he wishes until sunset.'

His saying (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, that is for the obligatory fast,' means the making up of the obligatory fast, because the obligatory fast itself does not have the choice to break it at any time.
ai.seo_question: Can a person break their voluntary fast at any time during the day?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the juristic distinction between obligatory and voluntary fasting. While the primary obligation of Ramadan or its *Qada* does not permit breaking the fast once commenced, the voluntary *Nafl* fast grants the individual the discretion to break it at any time before sunset, reflecting the flexibility inherent in supererogatory acts.
